case.pattern_description: A single rare device profile (Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720) carries transactions for 5 different cards belonging to unrelated customers inside a 30-day window, 100% of every card that profile has ever been seen with (5 in total). There is no testing sequence, no shared billing region and no single compromised cardholder: the common element is the machine. The bank's model scored the cluster a median of 0.71, so none of it was flagged individually and it is only visible by traversing the device profile out to its neighbouring cards. It affects every cardholder on that device, and fits none of the five documented typologies.

R6. Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

Pattern 3 Card-not-present fraud from a new device. Same as above, with the identity record marking the device as `New` for this account, sometimes behind a proxy. Stronger than pattern 2, still not proof: people buy new phones.

The activity was conducted online under product code R, billed in region 264.0, from device profile 'Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720' which the identity record marks 'New' for this account. Device profile 'Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720' carries 5 distinct cards across unrelated customers inside a 30-day window (5 cards on this profile in the whole dataset, 100% of them in this window). Transactions cluster on product code(s) R x5 and the bank's model scored them a median of 0.71, so the cluster is invisible to the score. Device profile 'Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720': device profile not seen on this card before; identity record marks the device 'New' for this account. The same device profile carries transactions for C01104-K1, C01983-K1, C06224-K1, C11309-K1, cards belonging to customers with no relationship to one another, which indicates a single actor operating across multiple cardholders rather than an isolated compromise. A single rare device profile (Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720) carries transactions for 5 different cards belonging to unrelated customers inside a 30-day window, 100% of every card that profile has ever been seen with (5 in total). There is no testing sequence, no shared billing region and no single compromised cardholder: the common element is the machine. The bank's model scored the cluster a median of 0.71, so none of it was flagged individually and it is only visible by traversing the device profile out to its neighbouring cards. It affects every cardholder on that device, and fits none of the five documented typologies. Prior closed investigations CC-2011, CC-2087, CC-2860 connected to the same card or device profile were reviewed and support this assessment. Assessed fraud probability is 0.75. Actions recorded: BLOCK_CARD, CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS, ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST. Total suspicious amount: $99.92. This report is filed under the institution's fraud policy section 3a; the activity connects to a shared device profile / region cluster; the activity connects to another card's fraud; R9: the pattern is undocumented and shows coordinated abuse across customers.
